questions.question: What is the Data class (define) in Ruby?
questions.title: The Data Class (define)
questions.direct_answer: Data (Ruby 3.2+) defines immutable value objects: `Point = Data.define(:x, :y)` creates a class with a generated initialize and #== based on values (like Struct, but immutable and value-equal). p = Point.new(x: 1, y: 2) (or positional Point.new(1, 2)); p.x == 1; p == Point.new(1, 2) # true (value equality). Unlike Struct, Data objects are immutable — you can't reassign p.x = 5 (raises). They're perfect for value objects (points, money, config snapshots) where equality should be by value, not identity. Data.define(:x, :y) also accepts a block to add methods. Use Data over Struct when you want immutability and value equality; use Struct when you need mutation or a plain mutable record. Great for thread-safe, hashable, comparable value objects.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Data.define (Ruby 3.2+) creates immutable value objects with value equality, and how it differs from Struct.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Trying to mutate a Data object (raises — they're immutable), or using Struct when you want value equality + immutability.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Data.define(:x,:y) (Ruby 3.2+) -> immutable value objects; #== by value. Point.new(x:1,y:2). Use over Struct for immutability + value equality.

sections.title: Data.define
sections.content:
```ruby
# Ruby 3.2+: define an immutable value object
Point = Data.define(:x, :y)

p = Point.new(x: 1, y: 2)   # keyword args
p = Point.new(1, 2)        # positional also works

p.x            # 1
p.y            # 2
p == Point.new(1, 2)  # true  (VALUE equality, like Struct)

# IMMUTABLE (unlike Struct):
# p.x = 5            # raises NoMethodError (no setter)

# With a block (add methods):
Money = Data.define(:amount, :currency) do
  def to_s; "#{amount} #{currency}"; end
end
m = Money.new(100, 'USD')
m.to_s         # '100 USD'

# Use as hash keys (value objects are hashable):
{ Point.new(1,2) => 'a' }   # works (hash/eql based on values)

# Data vs Struct:
#   Data:   immutable, value-equal   -> value objects
#   Struct: mutable, identity-ish    -> plain mutable records
# Use Data for thread-safe, comparable value objects (points, money, config).
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Trying to mutate a Data object (raises — they're immutable).
Using Struct when you want immutability + value equality (use Data).
Forgetting Data needs Ruby 3.2+ (older Ruby: use Struct or a class).

Use Data over Struct for immutability + value equality; Struct for mutable records.
